title: perf(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions and rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
body:
Context and motivation: We want continuous, automated detection of performance regressions (latency and throughput) during canary rollouts and an enforceable set of rollout guards to automatically halt or rollback when SLOs are violated. This PR implements a detection pipeline that compares canary and baseline distributions for p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput (QPS), uses adaptive thresholds with hysteresis, and wires those signals into the rollout controller.

High level changes: 1) Add a metrics detector service (services/perf-detector) that ingests canary and baseline time-series (Prometheus via remote-read) and computes distribution-aware regressions using bootstrap/resampling and KS/Wasserstein tests. 2) Add a rollout guard layer to the canary controller (services/rollout-controller) to enforce failure/abort criteria with configurable hysteresis and minimum sample windows. 3) Expose new canary config fields in the API and Helm chart (chart/values.yaml) so teams can opt-in and tune sensitivity. 4) Add alerting and dashboard templates (observability/dashboards/perf-canary.jsonnet) and integration tests + load tests.

Design notes: - Detection uses both absolute and relative thresholds: absolute (e.g. p95 > 1200ms) and relative (p95_canary > 1.15 * p95_baseline). The detector computes confidence via bootstrap and only flags when p < 0.01. - Hysteresis: we require N consecutive windows (default 3) before the controller marks the canary unhealthy. Windows are 60s by default and configurable. This reduces noisy aborts on short spikes. - Minimum sample size: a canary must have at least 500 requests across the window to be considered for detection. - Fallback behavior: when detector fails (missing metrics, timeouts), controller falls back to conservative behavior: pause rollout and mark for manual review. - Compatibility: implemented backwards-compatible feature flags; default off for existing rollout configs.

Files/areas changed (summary): services/perf-detector/ (new) - detector service + unit tests; services/rollout-controller/ - integrate detector client and guard logic; api/schema/canary.yaml - new fields for thresholds/hysteresis; helm/redwood/templates/rollout-canary.yaml and chart/values.yaml - chart changes; observability/dashboards/perf-canary.jsonnet - dashboard; tests/e2e/perf_canary_flow_test.go - e2e tests with synthetic workloads; infra/ci - added perf-detector test job.

Checklist: - [x] Detector prototype implemented and unit tested. - [x] Controller integration + integration tests. - [x] Helm values and API schema bumped. - [x] Dashboards and alerts added. - [x] Load tests: synthetic traffic test shows detector detects injected +20% p95 regressions reliably. - [x] Docs: short runbook and API docs added.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests: detector statistics, edge cases (low sample counts), timeout paths. - Integration tests: spin up a baseline and canary using perf harness and validate detection and abort flows. - Load test: 3k RPS synthetic test where we injected a 25% p95 regression in the model; detector flagged in 3 consecutive windows and rollout controller paused as expected. - CI: new integration job added, flakey tolerances tuned.

Rollout plan: Ship behind feature flag perf_canary_autodetect (off by default). Gradual opt-in for internal services for 2 weeks, monitor for false positives with a dashboard. If stable, enable as default for new canaries in 6 weeks.

Backward/forward compatibility: No breaking API changes; new canary fields are optional. Helm chart change is additive.

Related work: ENG-2048 (perf canary design), ENG-2065 (rollout guard requirements).

Notes for reviewers: Looking for feedback on the threshold defaults and hysteresis parameters. Also sanity-check on the fallback semantics when metrics are unavailable.

review_comments: Liam Nguyen: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: add explicit unit test covering KS vs Wasserstein selection and add a short note in the runbook about expected false positive rate.
Asha Patel: Added unit tests for KS/Wasserstein selection and expanded runbook section on FP expectations (see docs/runbooks/perf-canary.md).
Carlos Gomez: Requesting change: default minimum sample size of 1000 is safer for our production traffic — suggest making this configurable but default to 1000.
Asha Patel: Updated default to 1000 and made it configurable via helm values and API schema. Kept tests updated.
Maya Singh: CI flake observed in the e2e harness — looks like a race in test teardown. Please retry CI and add a small sleep in teardown.
Asha Patel: Added a deterministic wait and re-ran CI. All integration tests passed on second run.
Liam Nguyen: Approved after changes. Carlos Gomez: Approved. Maya Singh: Approved.
release_notes: Add optional automatic performance regression detection for canary rollouts with configurable hysteresis and abort/rollback guards. Disabled by default behind perf_canary_autodetect feature flag.
